binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, implicitly bound in the Lean declaration.
h and epsilon are arbitrary real numbers.
scheme and perturbation are arbitrary functions from Fin n to the real numbers, equivalently arbitrary real vectors with n coordinates.
conclusions: sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of (h^2 * scheme(i) + (epsilon * h^2) * perturbation(i))^2) <= h^2 * (sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of scheme(i)^2) + |epsilon| * sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of perturbation(i)^2)).
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is identified with the coordinate set {0, 1, ..., n-1}; it is empty when n = 0.
For a vector x : Fin n -> Real, define ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x(i)^2).
Define the vector q coordinatewise by q(i) = h^2 * scheme(i) + (epsilon * h^2) * perturbation(i).
Here h^2 means h * h, and |epsilon| means max(epsilon, -epsilon).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural-number dimension n, every pair of real numbers h and epsilon, and every two real n-dimensional vectors scheme and perturbation, the Euclidean norm of the vector h^2 times scheme plus epsilon times h^2 times perturbation is at most h^2 times the sum of the Euclidean norm of scheme and |epsilon| times the Euclidean norm of perturbation.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There are no hypotheses: n may be zero, h and epsilon may have any real values, and the two vectors are unrestricted.
When n = 0, all three vectors have no coordinates, all sums are empty, and the conclusion degenerates to 0 <= 0.
When h = 0, both sides are zero, so the conclusion again degenerates to equality.
No positivity, nonzero, boundedness, or smallness condition is imposed on h or epsilon; epsilon appears without absolute value on the left and as |epsilon| on the right.

The proposition encodes only an exact real Euclidean-norm inequality. It does not encode floating-point computation, rounding, an approximation algorithm, componentwise perturbation bounds, normalization, equality conditions, or sharpness.
